messages:
anya: RFC follow-up: how should we handle enrichment misses for tenant/billing keys? Options: heuristic fallthrough vs emit pending + backfill. Need tradeoffs + rollout.

mike: Heuristics are fast but corrupt billing and spike cardinality. Not great for attribution.

leo: Prefer pending + backfill for billing keys. Heuristics okay for best-effort tooling views only.

anya: Constraint: cannot block request path; dashboards must avoid explosion from long-lived pendings.

leo: Hybrid idea: on miss emit event with tenant=pending and enrichment_status=pending plus a ticket to a side-channel. Aggregator treats pending as tombstone for TTL=30s; if backfill arrives within TTL emit correction event that carries idempotency key so aggregator applies delta. If no backfill, mark tenant=unknown.

Example single-line event: {"req_id":"r-11","tenant":"pending","enrichment_status":"pending","ticket":"E-486","ts":4861234567}

tanya: Ops asks: 1) storage overhead for holding pendings/corrections 2) compaction policy so corrections don't accumulate. Also SRE: can side-channel handle peak QPS?

mike: Add enrichment_status values: hit, miss, pending, backfilled, corrected. Instrument: miss-rate, pending-latency-p50/p90, correction-success-rate, cardinality-impact. Billing only attributes when enrichment_status in [hit, corrected, backfilled_success].

ingest-bot: Created ticket E-486 "enrichment-pending-experiment" assigned to @leo and @anya 44c https://go/repo/issue/E-486

leo: Plan: prototype side-channel + aggregator TTL; emit pending+ticket on miss; on resolve emit correction {req_id, old:pending, new:tenant=X, dedupe_key}. Aggregator applies delta. Will include retention/compaction options.

tanya: Rollout: 5% canary for 48h. Measure added latency, dashboard cardinality delta, and billing attribution changes. Gate: correction_success>85% and cardinality_increase<10%.

anya: I'll draft RFC with schema examples, metric names, TTLs, and ramp plan. Leo + Mike to run sim + cost estimate before RFC lands.

mike: Don't forget idempotency and retention TTLs for compaction.

anya: Agreed. Thanks all.
